short_description: 100 easy, screen-free plays for babies, toddlers and preschoolers, sorted by age. Every play: what you need, prep and mess icons, a talk line and a safety note.
long_description:
A cup, a box, a sock, or nothing at all. 100 Screen-Free Plays gives you a quick play for every age and every moment of an ordinary day, from first smiles to "and then what happened?"

The plays are sorted into four color-coded age bands (0–1, 1–2, 2–3 and 3–5). Each chapter opens with a one-page "at a glance" guide and a play-basket list, so you can start with your child's stage and look one band either side.

Every play has the same easy parts: what you need, prep and mess icons, where it works best, simple steps, a "Grow it" idea for next time, a "talk while you play" line and a safety note. The talk lines use six plain, everyday talk moves, such as pausing and waiting, saying what you see and offering a choice.

You'll also find a Safety first page, a Quick finder for bath time, rainy days, kitchen time, car rides and wind-down, a sample screen-free day, low-energy plays for tired grown-ups, and friendly, guilt-free ideas for when screens are on anyway. Tick off favorites on the 100-play tracker and plan the week on the play-week planner.

The PDF edition is full color in US Letter and A4, with blank play cards and planners you can type into in any free PDF reader. The paperback has a black-and-white interior to keep the price low.

Parent education, not medical advice. Every play is meant to be done with a grown-up right there.

compliance_notes: Brand rules checked (brand/BRAND.md, ops/COMPLIANCE-GATE.md). No health or medical claims: the book is described as parent education and makes no outcome or development claims. None of the banned diagnosis or clinical words from BRAND.md rule 1 and its search-targeting rule appear in the book, listing or keywords (checked by text search), and no clinical authorship is implied (the Sources page says the ideas are general parent education, not professional or clinical advice). Talk strategies are in plain words only (pause and wait, say what you see, repeat and add one, offer a choice, follow their lead, sing and gesture); no trademarked program names. No brands, apps, devices, shows, schools or companies are named; the only tablet shown is the brand's generic sleeping tablet. Research: only allowed citations are used (WHO 2019 guidelines; AAP 'Media and Young Minds' 2016; Brushe et al., JAMA Pediatrics 2024), stated as links, not causes. Child safety (rule 4): every play has its own safety note; for under-3s nothing smaller than a toilet-paper tube (the posting box, sorting, cups, cars and stacking plays all say so); no balloons (and the Safety page says no balloons under 8); no cords or strings long enough to wrap a neck (the tightrope play uses tape, the pasta play says 'towers, not necklaces', dress-up says no cords around necks, bedtime play says keep blind cords out of reach); every water play says stay within arm's reach and tip water out; food plays exclude whole grapes, nuts, popcorn, raw apple and hard candy; small items (dry pasta, play dough, small toy animals) appear only in the 3–5 band with a warning to keep them from younger siblings. Poison Control number (1-800-222-1222, US) and 911 are standard public numbers. Zero-shame tone on the screens page. Copyright line: '© 2026 AlphaPlay LLC. Play Before Pixels is a trade name of AlphaPlay LLC.' on the copyright page, sources page, back cover and listing images. Print: the PDFs are RGB; the paperback interior is converted to grayscale for KDP's black-and-white option. Chromium embeds the brand's variable web fonts as Type 3 outline fonts; text stays vector, but run KDP's previewer and check for font warnings [VERIFY]. The final files must be checked against the chosen printer's current template (KDP, IngramSpark, Lulu, etc.) before upload, including the interior size and the cover spine width (0.1847 in here for 82 pages on white paper, from KDP's 0.002252 in per page) [VERIFY with KDP's cover calculator]. The spine carries no text because KDP only allows spine text on books over 79 pages with 0.0625 in clearance each side, and this spine is too thin for that; a 150-play second edition will be thick enough for a matching spine title. Human authorship: the text and art were drafted with AI assistance. The founder's own rewrites (see human_todo) are the human-authored part; do not describe AI-drafted material as human-authored in any copyright filing, and answer KDP's AI-content questions truthfully.
